Article Title: US government memo said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Megaspeed’s Alice Huang; she is believed to be a spy recruited by Chinese ministry; lawmakers now have questions on...
Article Text:
US memo links Jensen Huang to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang

Megaspeed bought billions in Nvidia hardware while Alice Huang was a top executive

Three House committees want Jensen Huang to explain his Megaspeed ties on November 18

US security officials are frustrated by Huang’s lobbying for China chip sales

US officials believe Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who American intelligence thinks was recruited to spy for China, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter.The claim comes from a government memo written earlier this year using information gathered by US intelligence. According to the FT, it was shared with a small group of top officials shortly before President Donald Trump travelled to Beijing for his May summit with Xi Jinping . Alice Huang is believed to have been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security, the country’s main spy agency.Nvidia declined to comment on the memo or the claim of an intimate relationship. The company has previously said Huang meets “thousands of customer executives every year.” The White House and the CIA also declined to comment, and Alice Huang could not be reached. Neither she nor Megaspeed has been charged with a crime. The two Huangs are not related.Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen. She was listed as Megaspeed’s managing director for its first eight months and has described herself as its CEO, though she has since left.The company was spun off in 2023 from 7Road, a Chinese gaming and cloud firm partly owned by the Chinese government.Washington has been watching Megaspeed since late 2024. That year, a Commerce Department official visited its Malaysian data centre and found Nvidia equipment still packed in boxes, which suggested the hardware was passing through rather than being installed. The New York Times, citing trade records, reported that Megaspeed’s Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion of advanced AI equipment with Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026.Nvidia says its own checks found no evidence of chips being diverted to China.The two executives have been photographed together more than once: at a Taipei bar with a group of customers around Computex in June 2024, and leaving a Taipei restaurant after a business dinner in May 2025.The FT report landed a day after three Republican chairmen asked Huang to sit for a joint, closed-door briefing. Brian Mast of the Foreign Affairs Committee, John Moolenaar of the Select Committee on China and Rick Crawford of the Intelligence Committee want him to discuss his interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s safeguards against foreign espionage.“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk,” they wrote.The request is voluntary, not a subpoena. It follows a New York Times report last month that US spy agencies learned of the relationship by surveilling Alice Huang. Huang has described his dealings with her as normal business and said the US government never told him about its suspicions.It also marks a shift for Republican leaders, who have mostly followed Trump’s hands-off line on tech. Anti-tech sentiment largely helped Democrats in the midterms, and Senator Elizabeth Warren has renewed her call for Huang to testify.The allegations land on a CEO with rare access to the White House. National security officials have privately voiced frustration with Huang, who personally lobbied Trump this year to let Nvidia sell its H200 chip to Chinese customers, the FT reported.Huang has met Trump several times since his second term began. When Trump left for Beijing in May, Huang was not among the CEOs on Air Force One. Trump called him after learning this, and Huang flew to Alaska to board the presidential jet during a stopover. In September, he attended Trump’s state dinner for Xi.The Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment. Beijing has previously called claims that it was spying on Nvidia groundless.So far, the memo has reached Capitol Hill only through press reports. Huang has until Wednesday, November 11, to tell lawmakers whether he will answer questions about it in person.
Article Summary: Three House committees want Jensen Huang to explain his Megaspeed ties on November 18. US security officials are frustrated by Huang’s lobbying for China chip sales.Megaspeed bought billions in Nvidia hardware while Alice Huang was a top executive.

Article Title: As Oracle makes a 'will not do' pledge to worried investors; analysts say company is trying to show that there's a method to the madness in ...
Article Text:
As Oracle makes a 'will not do' pledge to worried investors; analysts say company is trying to show that there's a method to the madness in ..

Oracle becomes a concern for investors

Oracle to cut back on outside financing

Last month, Oracle told its investors that it will not raise more than $20 billion in additional financing for AI through fiscal 2030. According to a Reuters report then, the pledge is meant to reassure worried investors that the company led by Larry Ellison will need ever-larger ‌sums of outside money to fund its aggressive data-center buildout. Speaking at the company’s investor day in Las Vegas, CFO Hilary Maxson said Oracle also expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028. It is expected to top $30 billion in fiscal 2029, as the capital spending declines. Following the announcement, Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne, as quoted in Reuters report, said: “Oracle is trying to show investors that there's a method to the madness of its massive AI infrastructure spending”."Though ⁠the projections are ambitious and far from guaranteed, they demonstrate an understanding of investors' concerns and offer an optimistic path toward ​addressing them."As stated in the report, Oracle has become a major concern in the AI industry because it does not have the large and steady revenue streams of cloud giants such as Microsoft and Amazon. It also depends heavily on OpenAI , the ChatGPT maker that is still losing money.The deal with OpenAI has added hundreds of billions of dollars in future cloud business to Oracle’s order book. However, building the data centres and other infrastructure needed to meet these commitments has pushed Oracle to rely heavily on borrowing money and selling shares.In October, Oracle said it plans to reduce its initial spending by using vendor financing, hardware provided by customers and advance payments from customers. These steps are expected to help the company manage its cash needs until it starts generating positive free cash flow. The company also expects to stop depending on external funding for its growth from fiscal 2029. It also forecasts that its net debt will fall to less than 3.5 times its annual core earnings that year.Earlier this year, Oracle said it planned to raise $40 billion through debt and stock sales during the current financial year. This included a $20 billion stock sale that it completed in the first quarter. As of August 31, Oracle had $125.34 billion in debt and other borrowings, while its cash and cash equivalents stood at around $36.37 billion."I've told you we ​need an additional up ⁠to $20 billion in funding for the remainder of our fiscal 2027," Maxson said."We're announcing that this $20 billion, split evenly between debt and equity, is the final amount needed to fund the remainder of ​this cycle."
Article Summary: Oracle has become a major concern in the AI industry because it does not have the large and steady revenue streams of cloud giants such as Microsoft and Amazon. It also depends heavily on OpenAI, the ChatGPT maker that is still losing money. The company expects to stop depending on external funding for its growth from fiscal 2029.

Article Title: America's Delaware state's proposal to run AI Agents run companies and not human CEOs, to be investigated, Governor Matt Meyer gets 'complaint letter' asking how ...
Article Text:
A representative picture.

Dear Governor Meyer:

James Comer, Chairman, Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

Delaware state's proposal to let companies be operated by AI agents is facing protest. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.) is investigating the State of Delaware’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC). Under the proposal, an AI Agent would an AI agent would run day-to-day operations of a corporate entity while providing the human or entity behind the AIC with liability protections from potential harms to consumers, the public, and business partners perpetuated by the controlling AI.In a letter to Delaware Governor Matt Meyer, Chairman Comer requests documents and information on the state’s assessed risks of this initiative, as well as the forces driving Delaware and other states to adopt such proposals. Read the letter:The Committee on Oversight and Government Reform seeks assistance obtaining documents related to your state administration’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity to be known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC). According to your Secretary of State, an AIC would be run day-to-day by an artificial intelligence (AI) agent while providing the human or entity capitalizing the AIC with liability protections from potential harms to business partners, consumers, and the public, perpetrated by the controlling AI “except where [the capitalizer] fails to capitalize the company or uses it to commit fraud or a willful violation of law.While this Committee has promoted2 the importance and potential of AI technologies to benefit U.S. citizens, the work of governments, and the global economy, it has also conducted oversight examining uses of artificial intelligence that may be harmful, unfair, or non-transparent to consumers or other businesses through surveillance pricing, assessment of housing fees, and for rental car damage billing. We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives.On July 23, 2025, you signed Delaware House Joint Resolution, which directed Delaware’s Artificial Intelligence Commission to work with your appointed Secretary of State Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez to create “a regulatory sandbox framework for the testing of innovative and novel technologies that utilize agentic artificial intelligence.” The resolution directed the state AI Commission, in collaboration with the Secretary of State, to deliver a written report of findings and recommendations no later than January 2, 2026. The subsequent report of the Delaware Artificial Intelligence Commission addressed to you and other state officials on December 22, 2025, noted that a Commission subcommittee is “actively working towards a draft regulatory framework that would create a regulatory sandbox that would test and evaluate agentic artificial intelligence and its application to corporate governance.”7 The twopage report referencing House Joint Resolution 7 did not mention any commission efforts to assess the potential safety, harms, risks, or outside consultations with independent experts associated with the proposal.In late June 2026, authors released a draft 36-page legislative proposal that is reportedly “likely to be introduced in the General Assembly next year.”9 John Mark Zeberkiewicz, a lawyer whose biography at Delaware based firm Richards, Layton, & Finger describes him as having represented Facebook (now Meta) and other clients focused on “complex transactional matters involving Delaware corporations, including mergers and acquisitions, corporate governance, and corporate finance” is described as the “principal drafter of the proposed legislation. ” According to Zeberkiewicz, “Anything that a company can do, the AIC can do as a company.”He further specified this would include allowing AI agents to engage in just about any business activity from providing coding services to filing lawsuits and would protect owners of new AICs fromfacing legal liability from actions the AI might take.13 Delaware Secretary of State PatibandaSanchez, in a joint op-ed with an AI company CEO contributing to the project wrote, “Delaware sees this and intends to set the norms for governing AI agents. The legal system has admitted new kinds of actors before. The stakes are higher now, and the timeline shorter with AI capabilities rapidly advancing. We invite the companies building agentic systems to develop the AIC framework with us. ”14 Patibanda-Sanchez was also quoted the same month on the importance of the proposal for positioning Delaware as a haven for registering companies, “Should a new entity form be created out of it, that’s a really huge benefit to our state’s revenues.”One Delaware media outlet reporting on the proposal noted, “It is not immediately clear whether any large company or lobbying group asked Delaware to propose its AI testing ground.”16 In September 2026, a different media outlet noted the Delaware Secretary of State’s office declined to answer questions about the nature of the state’s working relationship with an AI company contributing to the proposal.While Delaware officials tout the benefits of an AIC regulatory framework for creating transparency around the decision making of an agentic AI, such transparency does not appear to exist in this policy making initiative that may soon result in new state law. The Committee seeks information regarding how Delaware has considered the risks of this initiative as well as the forces driving Delaware, and possibly other states, to adopt such proposals to inform possible federal legislative efforts including proposals to appropriately limit state AI regulatory initiatives.To assist the Committee’s oversight of this matter, we request the following information, covering the time period January 1, 2025, to the present, unless otherwise indicated, as soon as possible but no later than November 9, 2026:1. All documents and communications, including those to or from non-government entities or persons, including internal AI chat logs, held by your administration regarding policy development efforts or inputs for AIC and any other discussion about artificial intelligence and liability;2. All ethics, consulting, and other agreements completed by contributors from outside government to AIC policy development;3. All documents and communications, including those with all individuals or entities consulted, regarding possible safety concerns and harms related to AIC and efforts to limit liability for artificial intelligence;4. All drafts and all comments and inputs provided for all AIC policy proposals and proposal outlines considered by state officials. The Committee on Oversight and Government Reform is the principal oversight committee of the U.S. House of Representatives and has broad authority to investigate “any matter” at “any time” under House Rule X.18 House Rule X also provides the Committee jurisdiction to study intergovernmental relationships including those of states. To arrange for the delivery of documents, or if you have any questions, please contact Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Majority staff at (202) 225-5074.
Article Summary: Delaware state's proposal to let companies be operated by AI agents is facing protest. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.) is investigating the State of Delaware’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC)

Article Title: When Jeff Bezos on stage shared what world's biggest investor Warren Buffet said when he asked him why people don't 'exactly copy' his investment strategy
Article Text:
When Jeff Bezos on stage shared what world's biggest investor Warren Buffet said when he asked him why people don't 'exactly copy' his investment strategy

What Warren Buffett told Jeff Bezos about his investment strategy

Jeff Bezos also built Amazon with a long-term approach

Getting rich through investing is a goal many people share, but building wealth over decades requires patience. While some investors look for quick returns, Warren Buffett has long followed a strategy built around long-term investments and the power of compounding. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos once asked Warren Buffett why more people did not follow his investment approach, despite its simplicity. Buffett’s response, shared by Bezos at the America Business Forum in Miami in 2025, highlighted a key reason why many investors struggle to stay focused on long-term gains.“I once asked Warren Buffett, why don’t more people copy your investment strategy?” Jeff Bezos said on stage at the America Business Forum in Miami in 2025. “It’s not that difficult to understand in principle. And he said, ‘Oh, Jeff, that’s easy. My approach is a get-rich-slowly scheme.'”Jeff Bezos then explained why Buffett’s approach may be difficult for many people to follow.“And people don’t like those,” he continued. “But there’s a lot of truth in that for everything, which is if you can think in terms of seven years instead of three years, and you can defer gratification and think long term, that will give you a head start against all of your competitors because most people can’t do that.”Warren Buffett’s investment strategy has focused on buying strong businesses at reasonable prices and holding them for long periods. He has often stressed the importance of patience rather than trying to predict short-term market movements.In his 1988 letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, Buffett wrote, “Our favorite holding period is forever.” The approach relies on allowing investments to grow over time. Compounding can have a greater effect over longer periods, although investment returns are never guaranteed.Bezos has also spoken about the importance of thinking beyond short-term results. Amazon’s first shareholder letter in 1997 carried the heading “It’s All About the Long Term.”The company invested heavily in warehouses, technology and new businesses during its early years. Amazon reported its first full-year profit in 2003, six years after the letter was published.Bezos’ remarks in Miami reflected the same principle: focusing on a longer time horizon can offer an advantage when others are prioritising quicker results.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos once asked Warren Buffett why more people did not follow his investment approach, despite its simplicity. Buffett’s response highlighted a key reason why many investors struggle to stay focused on long-term gains. Warren Buffett has long followed a strategy built around long- term investments and the power of compounding.

Article Title: World’s most valuable company CEO loses spot in world’s top 10 richest, loses $15 billion in a day
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

$2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq in one day

Why tech companies lost billions recently

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang lost his place in the world’s top 15 richest billionaires. According to Bloomberg, the tech billionaire lost nearly $15.1 billion in a day after the company’s stocks tumbled following Democrats’ sweeping victories in the midterm election. The loss dropped him to 13th from ninth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Other billionaires whose wealth declined were Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Oracle founder Larry Ellison, who lost $79.7 billion and $10.1 billion, respectively.The decline comes after the Nasdaq 100 index erased $2.5 trillion in market value in a single day on November 5 as Nvidia and other major technology companies suffered steep losses amid growing fears over the future of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending in the US. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.5% on Thursday, marking its biggest one-day drop since the market sell-off triggered by US President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025.The fall hit major tech companies include Nvidia and AMD whose shares dropped by 9% and 17% during Thursday’s trading session. Notably, Nvidia hit a market capitalization of $5.02 trillion earlier this week, regaining the title of world’s most valuable company from Apple.The Democrats’ strong performance in the US midterm elections has raised concerns that local opposition and tighter scrutiny could slow the construction of new data centres. Several incoming Democratic governors, including in Texas, have called for an immediate moratorium on data centre development.Data centres require large amounts of electricity and water, raising concerns among communities about pressure on power grids and local resources. UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of expected US data centre capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses.Analysts have warned that the AI boom may be entering a phase where companies are judged not just on their growth potential but also on the cost of building and operating their infrastructure.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang lost nearly $15.1 billion in a day after the company’s stocks tumbled following Democrats’ sweeping victories in the midterm election. The loss dropped him to 13th from ninth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Other billionaires whose wealth declined were Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Oracle founder Larry Ellison.

Article Title: Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards
Article Text:
Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards

Gigabyte has launched its Gigabyte 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign to mark its 40th anniversary, offering consumers a chance to win Amazon gift vouchers, monitors, AORUS merchandise and other products. The campaign will run from November 1 to December 31, 2026, and is open to residents of India. The campaign will feature three activities: Build a Rig, Play a Run and Share Your Story. Consumers can participate by purchasing eligible Gigabyte products, playing a browser-based game or sharing stories about their Gigabyte hardware.Under the Build a Rig activity, Gigabyte is offering rewards through its AORUS Full House programme. Consumers purchasing eligible Gigabyte and AORUS products can earn Amazon gift vouchers based on the number of product categories included in their PC build.The vouchers are worth up to Rs 15,500. Participants with complete builds can also receive AORUS merchandise, while select AORUS INFINITY products qualify for an additional bonus.The Play a Run activity features AORUS Infinity Run, a free browser-based game that takes players through five eras of hardware, from 1986 to the AI era.Each run lasts up to 90 seconds, and players do not need to log in. Participants can submit one entry per day after completing a run. Every valid entry will be included in a monthly random draw for a Gigabyte monitor.Players can also share their scorecards on Instagram by tagging @aorus_in and using the hashtag #MyGigabyte to participate in AORUS merchandise giveaways.The Share Your Story activity, called Still Running, invites consumers to share their experiences with Gigabyte products they have owned. Participants can write about hardware that remains in their PC, has been passed on to someone else or has been retired. Stories can be submitted on Instagram using @aorus_in and hashtags #MyGigabyte or #ENTERINFINITYINDIA, through the pinned Still Running thread on the r/aorusin Reddit community, or via an online form.More than 20 prizes are available, including at least three Gigabyte products. A Gigabyte India panel will select monthly winners across four categories: Best Story, Best Second Life, Most Loyal Builder and Still Running.The campaign activities opened on November 1, 2026, at 12am IST and will close on December 31, 2026, at 11:59pm IST. November winners will be announced in the first week of December 2026, while December winners will be announced in the first week of January 2027.Gigabyte said the campaign will run through its India community channels on Instagram and Reddit. Two of the three activities are free to enter, and participants can submit their stories in any language.Commenting on the campaign, Sunil Grewal, Director, Gigabyte India, said, “Forty years is a long time in an industry where hardware changes every year or two. What has carried us through is the trust of people who build their own PCs and expect them to keep running long after the build is done. ENTER INFINITY is our way of handing this anniversary to them. Whether someone is building a new rig this festive season, playing a quick run, or telling us about a Gigabyte motherboard that is still running years later, we want our next chapter in India to be shaped by those experiences.
Article Summary: Gigabyte launches 40 ENTER INFINITY India campaign with Amazon vouchers, monitors and gaming rewards. The campaign will run from November 1 to December 31, 2026, and is open to residents of India. Consumers can participate by purchasing eligible Gigabyte products, playing a browser-based game or sharing stories about their Gigabyte hardware.

Article Title: Group that attacked Microsoft datacenter site; warns of more protests: On November 6 and 7, 2026 we are taking action across 18 countries to stop ...
Article Text:
In this image made from video, protesters climb a crane at a site where a new Microsoft data center is being built, in Amsterdam, Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (AP Photo)

Protests planned across 16 countries

What 'Stop Dirty Data Centers' coalition says on its website

Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam faced breach from angry protestors in Amsterdam as they broke into the construction site. Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday, according to the "Stop Dirty Data ‌Centres" coalition, which is rallying environmental groups and digital rights campaigns behind calls to pause large-scale construction. Some carried placards with messages reading: "Screw your datacentre".Responding to protests, Microsoft said that it understood that people had strong feelings about the project and respected their right to express them peacefully but did not condone any unlawful actions.Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday, according to the "Stop Dirty Data Centers" coalition, which is rallying environmental groups and digital rights campaigns behind calls to pause large-scale construction. In Amsterdam on Friday, more than 100 activists gathered at the construction site of a Microsoft AI data centre, marching arm in arm before breaking into the site, climbing cranes, hanging balloons and dancing while police stood by. Some carried placards with messages reading: "Screw your datacenter."Site owner Pure Data Centers, which plans to invest more than $1 billion and is backed by Brookfield-owned Oaktree, said it was committed to engagement with local stakeholders."We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue about the development and any concerns they may have," it said. Other planned actions include a march in Dublin, a protest outside the parliament building in Warsaw, and a demonstration against a different Microsoft data centre in Denmark. [...] Stop Dirty Data Centers says it is not anti-progress or calling for existing data centers to be closed but that major construction should be halted until governments establish clearer rules.The Netherlands has about 200 data centres either planned, under construction or ​in operation.On 6-7 November 2026 we are taking action across Europe to say Stop Dirty Data Centres. Local communities are rising up to stop dirty data centres where they live. We will unite and exercise our democratic rights to speak out, assemble, and protest to hold elected officials to account. We’re calling for an immediate moratorium on large data centres in Europe!Making a call for action, the group says, "The explosion of AI data centres across our towns and cities is taking a toll that we can no longer afford. Join us and act now to prevent the irreparable harms data centres pose to the wellbeing of people and planet.""By coordinating our actions, we demonstrate the power we have to halt the unchecked expansion of AI data centres and prevent our democracy being taken hostage by big tech industry interests. Together we are calling on elected leaders to implement moratoria at local, national and European level that pause data centre construction until we, the people, have democratically decided what is needed to ensure AI and data centres serve people and the planet, not private greed," it adds.
Article Summary: Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday. In Amsterdam on Friday, more than 100 activists gathered at the construction site of a Microsoft AI data centre. Other planned actions include a march in Dublin, a protest outside the parliament building in Warsaw.

Article Title: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, who famously warned internet has become ‘less human’, now says AI ‘can cause a lot of harm’
Article Text:
Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian

The age of 'AI Slop' and dead internet

Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian believes the internet as we know it is fundamentally broken, and artificial intelligence (AI) is both a symptom and a driver of the shift. Speaking with WIRED at the inaugural WIRED World Fair recently, Ohanian warned that while AI holds massive promise, “there is still a very real chance that this technology can cause a lot of harm for sure. ” Ohanian also said that building traditional social media apps is “not cool anymore”, as much of the web has been compromised, leaving him searching for what comes next for user-generated content (UGC).Ohanian now leads the venture capital firm Seven Seven Six, which manages over $1.3 billion in assets. Lately, he has turned his attention to sports, an area where he still sees genuine, real-life communities thriving “in the age of AI slop” and a “manipulated” internet. He is an open proponent of the “Dead Internet Theory,” the idea that bots now generate a massive share of online content and activity. According to Ohanian, large language models have put this trend into overdrive, with AI agents rapidly outpacing real people.“The internet that I grew up on … that was really built for humans first; user interfaces and experiences are going to go away,” Ohanian said, explaining that the web is increasingly being built for AI agents rather than human users.The boom in generative AI has created a complicated reality for platforms like Reddit. On one hand, Reddit’s massive archive of human conversations has become a goldmine, leading to lucrative data-licensing deals with companies like Google and OpenAI to train their models. “Platforms like ours became very, very valuable to LLMs,” Ohanian noted.On the other hand, the technology is \ undercutting the business. Just last week, Reddit’s shares dropped 29% after the company warned that Google’s AI-powered search was eating into its referral traffic. Beyond the stock price, Ohanian worries that turning online discussions into a commercial product has ruined their authenticity, leaving them full of “bullshit.”“The internet has gotten so manipulated because it is so incredibly valuable to do so,” he said.To combat third-party data scraping and protect user engagement, Reddit recently announced it will require users to sign in. While Ohanian declined to say whether he supports that specific policy, he stressed that “there has to be provable humanity on the internet without being creepy.”
Article Summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian believes the internet as we know it is fundamentally broken. He believes artificial intelligence (AI) is both a symptom and a driver of the shift. Ohanian warned that while AI holds massive promise, “there is still a very real chance that this technology can cause a lot of harm for sure”

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have pledged to donate 99% of their Meta shares; here's the open letter they wrote to their eldest daughter Maxima in 2015; it makes a promises that ...
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg with his wife Priscilla Chan

Here's the open letter Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan wrote in 2015

A letter to our daughter

Dear Max,

Your mother and I don't yet have the words to describe the hope you give us for the future. Your new life is full of promise, and we hope you will be happy and healthy so you can explore it fully. You've already given us a reason to reflect on the world we hope you live in.

Like all parents, we want you to grow up in a world better than ours today.

While headlines often focus on what's wrong, in many ways the world is getting better.

Health is improving. Poverty is shrinking. Knowledge is growing. People are connecting. Technological progress in every field means your life should be dramatically better than ours today.

We will do our part to make this happen, not only because we love you, but also because we have a moral responsibility to all children in the next generation.

We believe all lives have equal value, and that includes the many more people who will live in future generations than live today.

Our society has an obligation to invest now to improve the lives of all those coming into this world, not just those already here.

But right now, we don't always collectively direct our resources at the biggest opportunities and problems your generation will face.

Consider disease. Today we spend about 50 times more as a society treating people who are sick than we invest in research so you won't get sick in the first place.

Medicine has only been a real science for less than 100 years, and we've already seen complete cures for some diseases and good progress for others. As technology accelerates, we have a real shot at preventing, curing or managing all or most of the rest in the next 100 years.

Today, most people die from five things -- heart disease, cancer, stroke, neurodegenerative and infectious diseases -- and we can make faster progress on these and other problems.

Once we recognize that your generation and your children's generation may not have to suffer from disease, we collectively have a responsibility to tilt our investments a bit more towards the future to make this reality. Your mother and I want to do our part.

Curing disease will take time. Over short periods of five or ten years, it may not seem like we're making much of a difference. But over the long term, seeds planted now will grow, and one day, you or your children will see what we can only imagine: a world without suffering from disease.

There are so many opportunities just like this. If society focuses more of its energy on these great challenges, we will leave your generation a much better world.

• • •

Our hopes for your generation focus on two ideas: advancing human potential and promoting equality.

Advancing human potential is about pushing the boundaries on how great a human life can be.

Can you learn and experience 100 times more than we do today?

Can our generation cure disease so you live much longer and healthier lives?

Can we connect the world so you have access to every idea, person and opportunity?

Can we harness more clean energy so you can invent things we can't conceive of today while protecting the environment?

Can we cultivate entrepreneurship so you can build any business and solve any challenge to grow peace and prosperity?

Promoting equality is about making sure everyone has access to these opportunities -- regardless of the nation, families or circumstances they are born into.

Our society must do this not only for justice or charity, but for the greatness of human progress.

Today we are robbed of the potential so many have to offer. The only way to achieve our full potential is to channel the talents, ideas and contributions of every person in the world.

Can our generation eliminate poverty and hunger?

Can we provide everyone with basic healthcare?

Can we build inclusive and welcoming communities?

Can we nurture peaceful and understanding relationships between people of all nations?

Can we truly empower everyone -- women, children, underrepresented minorities, immigrants and the unconnected?

If our generation makes the right investments, the answer to each of these questions can be yes -- and hopefully within your lifetime.

• • •

This mission -- advancing human potential and promoting equality -- will require a new approach for all working towards these goals.

We must make long term investments over 25, 50 or even 100 years. The greatest challenges require very long time horizons and cannot be solved by short term thinking.

We must engage directly with the people we serve. We can't empower people if we don't understand the needs and desires of their communities.

We must build technology to make change. Many institutions invest money in these challenges, but most progress comes from productivity gains through innovation.

We must participate in policy and advocacy to shape debates. Many institutions are unwilling to do this, but progress must be supported by movements to be sustainable.

We must back the strongest and most independent leaders in each field. Partnering with experts is more effective for the mission than trying to lead efforts ourselves.

We must take risks today to learn lessons for tomorrow. We're early in our learning and many things we try won't work, but we'll listen and learn and keep improving.

• • •

Our experience with personalized learning, internet access, and community education and health has shaped our philosophy.

Our generation grew up in classrooms where we all learned the same things at the same pace regardless of our interests or needs.

Your generation will set goals for what you want to become -- like an engineer, health worker, writer or community leader. You'll have technology that understands how you learn best and where you need to focus. You'll advance quickly in subjects that interest you most, and get as much help as you need in your most challenging areas. You'll explore topics that aren't even offered in schools today. Your teachers will also have better tools and data to help you achieve your goals.

Even better, students around the world will be able to use personalized learning tools over the internet, even if they don't live near good schools. Of course it will take more than technology to give everyone a fair start in life, but personalized learning can be one scalable way to give all children a better education and more equal opportunity.

We're starting to build this technology now, and the results are already promising.

Not only do students perform better on tests, but they gain the skills and confidence to learn anything they want. And this journey is just beginning. The technology and teaching will rapidly improve every year you're in school.

Your mother and I have both taught students and we've seen what it takes to make this work. It will take working with the strongest leaders in education to help schools around the world adopt personalized learning.

It will take engaging with communities, which is why we're starting in our San Francisco Bay Area community. It will take building new technology and trying new ideas. And it will take making mistakes and learning many lessons before achieving these goals.

But once we understand the world we can create for your generation, we have a responsibility as a society to focus our investments on the future to make this reality.

Together, we can do this. And when we do, personalized learning will not only help students in good schools, it will help provide more equal opportunity to anyone with an internet connection.

• • •

Many of the greatest opportunities for your generation will come from giving everyone access to the internet.

People often think of the internet as just for entertainment or communication. But for the majority of people in the world, the internet can be a lifeline.

It provides education if you don't live near a good school. It provides health information on how to avoid diseases or raise healthy children if you don't live near a doctor. It provides financial services if you don't live near a bank. It provides access to jobs and opportunities if you don't live in a good economy.

The internet is so important that for every 10 people who gain internet access, about one person is lifted out of poverty and about one new job is created.

Yet still more than half of the world's population -- more than 4 billion people -- don't have access to the internet.

If our generation connects them, we can lift hundreds of millions of people out of poverty. We can also help hundreds of millions of children get an education and save millions of lives by helping people avoid disease.

This is another long term effort that can be advanced by technology and partnership. It will take inventing new technology to make the internet more affordable and bring access to unconnected areas.

It will take partnering with governments, non-profits and companies. It will take engaging with communities to understand what they need. Good people will have different views on the best path forward, and we will try many efforts before we succeed.

But together we can succeed and create a more equal world.

• • •

Technology can't solve problems by itself. Building a better world starts with building strong and healthy communities.

Children have the best opportunities when they can learn. And they learn best when they're healthy.

Health starts early -- with loving family, good nutrition and a safe, stable environment.

Children who face traumatic experiences early in life often develop less healthy minds and bodies. Studies show physical changes in brain development leading to lower cognitive ability.

Your mother is a doctor and educator, and she has seen this firsthand.

If you have an unhealthy childhood, it's difficult to reach your full potential.

If you have to wonder whether you'll have food or rent, or worry about abuse or crime, then it's difficult to reach your full potential.

If you fear you'll go to prison rather than college because of the color of your skin, or that your family will be deported because of your legal status, or that you may be a victim of violence because of your religion, sexual orientation or gender identity, then it's difficult to reach your full potential.

We need institutions that understand these issues are all connected. That's the philosophy of the new type of school your mother is building.

By partnering with schools, health centers, parent groups and local governments, and by ensuring all children are well fed and cared for starting young, we can start to treat these inequities as connected. Only then can we collectively start to give everyone an equal opportunity.

It will take many years to fully develop this model. But it's another example of how advancing human potential and promoting equality are tightly linked. If we want either, we must first build inclusive and healthy communities.

• • •

For your generation to live in a better world, there is so much more our generation can do.

Today your mother and I are committing to spend our lives doing our small part to help solve these challenges.

I will continue to serve as Facebook's CEO for many, many years to come, but these issues are too important to wait until you or we are older to begin this work. By starting at a young age, we hope to see compounding benefits throughout our lives.

As you begin the next generation of the Chan Zuckerberg family, we also begin the

Chan Zuckerberg Initiative

to join people across the world to advance human potential and promote equality for all children in the next generation. Our initial areas of focus will be personalized learning, curing disease, connecting people and building strong communities.

We will give 99% of our Facebook shares -- currently about $45 billion -- during our lives to advance this mission. We know this is a small contribution compared to all the resources and talents of those already working on these issues.

But we want to do what we can, working alongside many others.

We'll share more details in the coming months once we settle into our new family rhythm and return from our maternity and paternity leaves. We understand you'll have many questions about why and how we're doing this.

As we become parents and enter this next chapter of our lives, we want to share our deep appreciation for everyone who makes this possible.

We can do this work only because we have a strong global community behind us.

Building Facebook has created resources to improve the world for the next generation. Every member of the Facebook community is playing a part in this work.

We can make progress towards these opportunities only by standing on the shoulders of experts -- our mentors, partners and many incredible people whose contributions built these fields.

And we can only focus on serving this community and this mission because we are surrounded by loving family, supportive friends and amazing colleagues. We hope you will have such deep and inspiring relationships in your life too.

Max, we love you and feel a great responsibility to leave the world a better place for you and all children. We wish you a life filled with the same love, hope and joy you give us. We can't wait to see what you bring to this world.

Love,

Mom and Dad
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan wrote an open letter to their daughter in 2015. Zuckerberg and Chan: "We want you to grow up in a world better than ours today" Zuckerberg: "Technological progress in every field means your life should be dramatically better"

Article Title: As $2.5 billion transferred from Binance in single transaction; how it cost hackers just $15; the massive cryptocurrency theft’s ‘big shock’
Article Text:
Cryptocurrency theft

How a ‘$15 transaction’ that cleared the vault

It took hackers just $15 to unlock access to $2.5 billion, followed by a matter of seconds to move the entire sum, to pull off the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. That striking reality sits at the center of the historic cryptocurrency theft from Binance, where attackers leveraged an advanced Ethereum feature to siphon roughly 40% of their total haul in one single transaction. This incident was part of a broader, sophisticated cyberattack that drained an estimated $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance, according to Bloomberg. The FBI has tied the breach to North Korea.Binance disclosed that the breach began when an engineer fell for a fake job posting and downloaded malicious code, granting the hackers entry into internal systems. What followed was a high-level exploitation of Ethereum’s underlying mechanics that allowed the intruders to move billions even while the exchange scrambled to lock down its operations.The central target was Binance 14, an active hot wallet used by the platform to handle regular customer withdrawals. Connected directly to online services, the wallet held massive balances of Ether, stablecoins and dozens of alternative tokens. Having breached Binance’s signing infrastructure, the attackers secured a valid cryptographic signature from the Binance 14 wallet. At around 8:20 p.m. UTC on October 29, they broadcasted instructions to the Ethereum network, paying roughly $15 in standard network gas fees.That $15 transaction did not move any cryptocurrency. Instead, it registered authorisation for the hackers' own software to operate the wallet.The negligible cost highlights how public blockchains function: Ethereum processing fees reflect the computational effort needed to run a piece of code and overall network demand – not the monetary value of the tokens inside an account. Modifying access rights on an account holding billions costs the exact same as doing so on an account holding a few dollars.Approximately three and a half minutes later, the attackers triggered their software to execute a single, sweeping transfer worth roughly $2.5 billion.The fast drain was caused by EIP-7702, an Ethereum improvement proposal introduced on May 7, 2025, during the network’s Pectra upgrade.Available for about 18 months, EIP-7702 was designed to streamline the user experience by giving standard crypto wallets programmable capabilities, like bundling multiple separate operations into a single step or allowing third parties to cover transaction fees. In everyday terms, it acts like appointing a concierge authorised to handle multiple errands without requiring sign-off on every task.Security analysts point out that EIP-7702 did not open the door on its own; the hackers had already infiltrated Binance's systems and compromised its signing credentials. However, the feature allowed the attackers' code to step directly into Binance 14's shoes.By using EIP-7702's bundling capabilities, the hackers consolidated the withdrawal into a single transaction that cleared 167,464 Ether, over 60 other cryptocurrencies, including roughly $1.6 billion worth of Tether (USDT) – the combined haul totaled approximately $2.5 billion.
Article Summary: Hackers used advanced feature to siphon roughly 40% of total haul in one transaction. Incident was part of a broader, sophisticated cyberattack that drained an estimated $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance. FBI has tied the breach to North Korea.

Article Title: Bill Gates thinks that policy like the 'rich tax' that created 'uproar' in California is the only solution in the AI age; says: We can’t expect philanthropy as …
Article Text:
Bill Gates thinks that policy like the 'rich tax' that created 'uproar' in California is the only solution in the AI age; says: We can’t expect philanthropy as …

Why Bill Gates thinks billionaires should pay more tax in the AI age

Bill Gates also wants robots to be taxed

AI, some believe could make the world’s richest people even wealthier, but Bill Gates believes governments will need to do more to ensure that its benefits reach everyone. The Microsoft co-founder has backed progressive wealth taxes, including taxes on billionaires, arguing that philanthropy alone cannot address the growing gap between rich and poor in the AI age. In a recent interview with the Financial Times, Bill Gates said governments should take the primary responsibility for tackling inequality. He warned that charitable giving, even from the world’s wealthiest individuals, cannot replace public policy or act as a safety net for people affected by economic changes.“The primary responsibility of dealing with inequality will always rest with governments,” Gates said. “We can’t expect philanthropy, which is voluntary in nature, to be the safety net.”Bill Gates believes AI could create enormous wealth, particularly for people who own shares in technology companies. However, these gains may not be distributed equally.Data from the US Federal Reserve cited in the report shows that the wealthiest 1% of Americans own more than half of the country’s stock market. This means that as AI companies grow and their share prices rise, a large share of the gains could go to already wealthy investors.Gates said tax systems would need to change to address this imbalance. “So, in a world of AI, there will have to be changes in tax systems, including the ability to tax people with huge wealth, the ability to tax billionaires,” he said.The billionaire has also committed to giving away virtually all his wealth, estimated at around $100 billion, through the Gates Foundation. The foundation is expected to spend the money over the next 20 years. However, Gates believes even large philanthropic efforts cannot fully address the inequality that AI may create.Notably, this is not the first time that Gates said about taxing AI. He has previously suggested that governments should consider taxing robots and AI systems that replace human workers.His argument is that companies currently pay payroll taxes when they hire people, while buying a robot can often be treated as a business expense. This, he believes, could encourage businesses to replace workers with machines.
Article Summary: Bill Gates believes governments should take the primary responsibility for tackling inequality in the AI age. The Microsoft co-founder has backed progressive wealth taxes, including taxes on billionaires. He has previously suggested that governments should consider taxing robots and AI systems that replace human workers.

Article Title: One of last remaining Chestnut Groves, planted in the 1970s from wild surviving American chestnuts, at risk of being wiped out by datacenter labelled as: 'Largest single AI infrastructure investments
Article Text:
Image credit: Nscale

“one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history, anchoring America’s compute foundation.”

Why the chestnut orchard matters

What happens to the trees under the development plan

“There’s never been a plan to and there will never be a plan to bulldoze or cut down the trees,”

American chestnut trees in West Virginia face an uncertain future. An orchard at the former Clements State Tree Nursery in Mason County, established in the 1970s from surviving wild trees, stands on land sought by AI infrastructure developer Nscale. Conservation concerns centre on whether the mature trees can survive a proposed relocation.Nscale describes its Monarch Compute Campus asThe company plans to invest more than $20 billion across a campus covering over 2,250 acres. State officials have announced a preservation plan, but chestnut specialists say moving the trees carries risks that require independent assessment.The original American chestnuts at Clements were planted in 1976. Researchers collected nuts from large surviving trees in West Virginia, Virginia and Maryland, hoping they carried some resistance to chestnut blight, the fungal disease that devastated the species.Many seedlings died, but some survivors now reach 60 feet. Nuts from the original planting established a second orchard in the 1990s, which has supplied seeds for restoration work across West Virginia for more than a decade.The American Chestnut Foundation describes Clements as a managed orchard that supports research, breeding, and seed production. Several chestnut species grow there, and the foundation distinguishes it from a naturally occurring wild population.West Virginia Public Broadcasting reported that the orchard contains roughly half a dozen surviving trees from the original planting and another 15 to 20 mature trees from the later planting. Although infected with blight, they continue producing nuts. Understanding their survival could help researchers working to restore American chestnuts.Last month, Governor Patrick Morrisey announced that the trees would be relocated within the property in late 2027, during their dormant season, under professional arborist supervision. Nscale would cover the cost, and access for collecting seeds and saplings would continue.Nscale has also rejected claims that it intends to destroy the orchard.senior vice president Pete Hollis told West Virginia Public Broadcasting. The broadcaster reported concerns from local advocates and tree specialists about root damage and the trees’ ability to withstand relocation while affected by blight.In an update from last month, the American Chestnut Foundation recommended an independent evaluation. It said it knew of no documented examples of successfully relocating mature American chestnut trees, leaving the feasibility of the proposed move unresolved.
Article Summary: American chestnut trees in West Virginia face an uncertain future. An orchard at the former Clements State Tree Nursery in Mason County, established in the 1970s from surviving wild trees, stands on land sought by AI infrastructure developer Nscale. Conservation concerns centre on whether the mature trees can survive a proposed relocation.

Article Title: Jack Dorsey has been renovating his sprawling $32 million mansion for over 14 years; his utlra-rich neighbours can't stop complaining
Article Text:
In pic: Jack Dorsey

Two properties, one long project

Sauna complex, plunge pool and rooftop gardens

Estate expands beyond a single property

A neighbourhood-wide building boom

Even in one of San Francisco's wealthiest neighbourhoods, money cannot always buy peace and quiet. Jack Dorsey, the Twitter co-founder and chief executive of fintech company Block, has spent nearly 14 years renovating and expanding his oceanfront properties in the exclusive Sea Cliff neighbourhood, a project that neighbours say has turned the area into a long-running construction zone, according to a report by the New York Post. Residents told the publication that the sounds of jackhammers, cement mixers and construction vehicles have become a fixture of daily life as work on Dorsey's luxury compound continues years after it began. “I've been listening to 24-7 construction noise in the distance for years now,” one resident told the Post anonymously. “One day it will end. I hope.”Dorsey, 49, who now leads financial technology company Block, owns two adjoining properties in the exclusive Sea Cliff enclave. They overlook the Pacific Ocean and the Golden Gate Bridge and cover a combined 1.21 acres on El Camino del Mar. According to SFGate, jackhammers, cement mixers and construction trucks have been heard in the area for over a decade. He bought the first property in February 2012 for $9.99 million. The 3,734-square-foot modernist home, built in 1965, originally had two bedrooms and two bathrooms. Construction began within months and has continued in various forms since.City records show a major redevelopment application filed in December 2013 proposed $3.7 million in improvements, including seismic upgrades, extra living space, roof decks and a planted roof. That permit alone took three and a half years to obtain. A 2020 redesign changed the windows, courtyard and exterior finishes, and was approved in July 2022. Later applications covered solar panels, landscaping, fire sprinklers, retaining walls, an underground water tank and a cold plunge pool.As per the report, the architectural plans seen by the local media suggests that the Dorsey is creating a highly customised retreat. The redesigned property consists of vegetation-covered roofs, reclaimed redwood cladding, extensive stonework and large ocean-facing windows. The standout feature of the luxurious property is a private hot tub connected to the primary bedroom, a steam room, plunge pool, gym, outdoor fire pit and an expansive sauna complex with its own dedicated access areas. The renovation plan also include dozens of solar panels and a sophisticated fire-protection system which need more than 100 sprinklers and a dedicated water line.The project grew even larger in 2018 when Dorsey acquired the neighbouring property for $21.9 million, bringing his total acquisition costs to approximately $31.9 million.The second home spans about 3,588 square feet and sits on more than half an acre. While restrictions separating the two properties have reportedly been removed, available plans do not indicate that the homes will be physically merged into a single structure.The expansion mirrors a broader trend among technology billionaires assembling large residential compounds. The New York Post noted that Mark Zuckerberg has purchased multiple neighbouring properties around Lake Tahoe, while Sam Altman has also expanded his real-estate footprint around his San Francisco residence.While Dorsey's project has attracted attention because of its longevity, it is not the only source of disruption in Sea Cliff. The affluent neighbourhood, which has been home to figures including late comedian Robin Williams, actress Sharon Stone, Salesforce co-founder Marc Benioff and investor Tom Steyer, is experiencing a broader construction surge.Planning records cited in the report indicate that at least 24 homes along the eight-block stretch of El Camino del Mar have filed building permits since the start of 2025. Recent observations by local media found scaffolding, construction crews and heavy equipment operating outside several multimillion-dollar residences. For some residents, the combination of luxury home renovations and constant tourism has become an unexpected downside of living in one of San Francisco's most exclusive enclaves.Despite the complaints, there is no indication that Dorsey's renovation project is nearing completion, leaving some neighbours hoping that the sounds of construction will eventually give way to the tranquillity usually associated with a multimillion-dollar oceanfront address.
Article Summary: Twitter co-founder and chief executive of fintech company Block, Jack Dorsey, owns two properties in San Francisco's exclusive Sea Cliff neighbourhood. Dorsey bought the first property in February 2012 for $9.99 million. Construction began within months and has continued in various forms since. Neighbours say the sounds of jackhammers, cement mixers and construction vehicles have become a fixture of daily life.

Article Text:
Michael and wife Susan Dell

How Michael Dell is helping SK chairman’s $711 million divorce

Dell’s link to SK Group

Michael Dell is putting $406 million into South Korea’s SK Group, buying shares from chairman Chey Tae-wo. According to a Reuters report, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has agreed the sale of a 1.34% stake in holding company SK Inc to an investment fund linked to Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell for 544 billion won ($406 million). The deal is part of Chey Tae-Won’s plan to raise 944 billion won through share sales to pay a divorce settlement to his former wife.Earlier this month, SK Inc said in ​a filing that Chey Tae-Won had agreed to sell 1.65 million shares, or a 2.26% stake for ​944 billion won. Of those, DFO Public Investments, L.P., a Delaware-based investment fund ​affiliated with DFO Management, the family investment office of Michael Dell, agreed to buy 972,493 SK ​Inc shares.The sale covers the bigger part of a 944 billion won ($711 million) share sale to fund the payout to Roh Soh-yeong, director of Seoul's Art Center Nabi and the daughter of former South Korean president Roh Tae-woo.The rest of the money will reportedly come from a price return swap with Korea Investment & Securities, a Seoul brokerage, covering 681,431 shares, or 0.94% of SK Inc., for about 400 billion won ($301 million). Both transactions are due to settle on November 2.Dell Technologies, a major supplier of AI servers and data ‌centre ⁠infrastructure, has business ties with SK Hynix, SK Group's memory chipmaking unit. It supplies chips for Dell's data center servers.Michael Dell, 61, has a net worth of about $241.3 billion, making him the world's fifth-richest person. His wealth has grown as Dell Technologies' shares have risen and through his large stake in chipmaker Broadcom. He received the Broadcom shares when he sold software company VMware to Broadcom in 2023.
Article Summary: Michael Dell is putting $406 million into South Korea’s SK Group, buying shares from chairman Chey Tae-wo. Dell Technologies, a major supplier of AI servers and data ‌centre ⁠infrastructure, has business ties with SK Hynix, SK Group's memory chipmaking unit.

Article Title: Melinda French Gates gives 'guided office tour' to show 'few things that bring me JOY'; expands on the sentiment that women ...
Article Text:
Ginsburg quote remains a source of inspiration

A reminder of progress for women

The artwork behind her desk

Focus on women’s health

Bill Gates ex-wife and philanthropist Melinda Gates has offered followers a glimpse inside her office, showcasing three personal items that she says bring her joy while also reinforcing her long-standing advocacy for women’s advancement and leadership. In a video shared on social media platform Instagram, the Gates showed the viewers what she described as tour of “a few things that bring me JOY in my office.” The video shared featured various items such as a figurine of late US Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, a vintage board game titled “The Exciting Game of Career Girls,” and a piece of artwork displaying the word “JOY.” As per an Inc. report, the video has been viewed by more than 1.2 million people.Among the items, French Gates highlighted a figurine gifted by her younger brother that honours Ginsburg, whom she described as a major influence. She used the item to draw attention to one of the late justice's most widely cited observations: “Women belong in all places where decisions are made.” According to the report, French Gates also displayed a framed version of the quote signed by Ginsburg.The message aligns closely with French Gates' philanthropic work, which has focused heavily on improving opportunities for women and families.Through Pivotal, the organisation she founded in 2015, she has directed significant investments toward women's health and gender equality initiatives. Earlier this year, she pledged an additional $215 million to the organisation, bringing her total commitment over the previous two years to $600 million to support areas including contraception and maternal healthcare, according to Pivotal.Another item featured in the office tour was “The Exciting Game of Career Girls,” a board game from the 1950s. The game, which depicts careers such as nurse, stewardess and teacher as desirable options for women, serves as a reminder of how opportunities have expanded over time, French Gates said. “It reminds me that we actually have made a lot of progress when you think about all the different types of careers women have these days,” she said, according to the report. The comments expand on a theme that has long shaped her public advocacy: increasing women's participation in leadership roles and decision-making positions across society.The final item in the office tour was a large artwork reading “JOY,” which hangs above her desk. According to French Gates, the letters are composed of numerous small human figures, symbolising the idea of shared happiness and community. “Each little blob represents a different person, and it's a representation of collective joy,” she said. “If we have joy in our lives, if we share it with somebody else, it doubles that joy. ” She added that the artwork frequently draws comments from people during video calls, with many noticing the word displayed behind her and responding positively to it.French Gates’s philanthropy centres on advancing women and families. In 2015 she founded Pivotal, an organisation focused on women’s health. Earlier this year she pledged an additional $215 million to it, bringing her total commitment over the past two years to $600 million, according to Pivotal’s website. The money is meant to expand global access to contraceptives and maternal care.
Article Summary: Melinda Gates shared a video of three personal items that she says bring her joy. The items include a figurine of late US Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, a vintage board game titled “The Exciting Game of Career Girls,” and a piece of artwork displaying the word “JOY.”

Article Title: In 2018, Elon Musk donated $480,350 for Flint school water filters and $423,000 to buy laptops for students; he also pledged that he would 'fund fixing the water in any house that has ...'
Article Text:
Elon Musk's donations during the Flint crisis

Clean drinking water returns to schools

Delays before rollout

Flint's recovery efforts continue

In 2018, the SpaceX CEO Elon Musk’s foundation donated about $480,000 to install water filtration systems in Flint, Michigan, schools, along with $423,000 for student laptops. The foundation funded 136 filtering stations that serve twelve school buildings. The donation came years after Flint’s water supply was contaminated with catastrophic levels of lead in 2014, when officials switched to a cheaper water source.Podcaster and former advisor to the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), Katie Miller also recently shared a post on X highlighting the impact of the project. In the post, she noted that the Musk Foundation donated ultraviolet water filtration systems and new drinking stations across all 12 Flint Community Schools buildings as well as the district's administration building. She also pointed out that the city separately provided free water filters for residential homes.The donation made by Elon Musk’s Foundation dates back to 2018, when the organisation contributed around $480,350 to fund water filtration systems for Flint schools and an additional $423,000 to purchase laptops for students. Around the same time, Musk also pledged that he would "fund fixing the water in any house in Flint that has water contamination above FDA levels," as the city continued to deal with the fallout from its water crisis.The water crisis at Flint started in 2014, when the officials switched to a cheaper water source, which led to widespread lead contamination of water that affected thousands of residents. The water crisis also led to national outrage and prompted support from charities, public agencies and private donors asking for help for the affected communities.According to a report by The Independent, students in Flint were eventually able to drink directly from school water fountains for the first time in years after the Musk-funded filtration systems became operational. The foundation donated 136 filtering stations that serve school buildings throughout the district. Speaking at a ceremony marking the rollout of the new fountains, Kevelin Jones, superintendent of Flint Community Schools, said access to clean water should be a basic necessity rather than something families have to struggle to obtain. Before the filtration systems were activated, the district had relied on bottled water for several years.The filtration systems use advanced technology designed to remove contaminants, including lead, from drinking water. Before being placed into service, they were tested by researchers from Kettering University and independent environmental experts to ensure they met safety standards.The project also faced a lot of challenges. The installation of the filtration stations faced a lot of delays and also needed reconfiguration before they could be implemented completely. Once fully functional, the students welcomed the change after years without access to drinking fountains. One of the students also told the local media that it felt "amazing" to finally have clean water available at school. This change marked a significant moment for the district as it had depended on bottled water since the beginning of the crisis.The residents however appreciated the support, but some community leaders also agreed that water filters alone cannot solve the bigger problems caused on the infrastructure due to this water crisis. Former Flint Mayor Karen Weaver said in 2018 that in order to completely restore the trust of the public we need to replace the damaged water infrastructure and also lead service lines throughout the city.Since then, Flint has continued its recovery efforts. City officials have reported significant progress in inspecting service lines and replacing thousands of lead and galvanized steel pipes as part of the long-term effort to restore confidence in the city's water system.
Article Summary: Elon Musk’s foundation donated $480,350 to Flint schools in 2018. The money was used to install water filtration systems and buy laptops for students. The donation came years after Flint's water supply was contaminated with catastrophic levels of lead in 2014.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman reacts to Delaware’s AI agent proposal, says it is ‘deeply concerning to …’
Article Text:
What is Delaware Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC)

Congress threatens intervention

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned against a legislative proposal in Delaware that would permit autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents to legally manage and operate corporate entities. Suleyman pushed back the state’s initiative, saying that granting legal corporate status to autonomous software demands extreme scrutiny, and calling it ‘deeply concerning’. Not just tech leaders, the proposal also sparked sharp backlash from federal lawmakers like Representative James Comer (R-Ky.), chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.“Deeply concerning to me... Delaware proposal to let agents run businesses... we should be very cautious here,” Suleyman stated on social media platform X (formerly Twitter). Quoting directly from the framework's core premise, Suleyman highlighted the far-reaching nature of the concept:“A Delaware AIC will be a separate legal entity whose day-to-day affairs are managed by an AI agent rather than a person. At the agent’s direction, the AIC can sue and be sued in its own name, hold and dispose of property, and incur obligations...”Delaware, widely recognised as America’s premier hub for corporate incorporations, is exploring a new business structure titled an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC). According to a draft bill that may go before the Delaware State Legislature, the framework aims to introduce a 30-month “regulatory sandbox” to pilot the concept, bringing in additional state revenue through corporate filing fees and taxes.Under the provisions of the draft bill, an AIC could operate with any lawful commercial purpose, whether for-profit or non-profit, with the sole explicit restriction being the business of banking. Moreover, an AI agent could be formally designated to oversee day-to-day affairs, enter into contracts, make commercial transactions, and direct business strategy without a human at the helm.At the direction of its designated AI agent, the company could hold or dispose of real and personal property, incur financial obligations, and initiate or face legal lawsuits in its own corporate name.The prospect of shielding corporate backers from AI misbehaviour has triggered an immediate counter-offensive in Washington. Last month, Representative Comer sent a formal inquiry to Delaware Governor Matt Meyer demanding documents regarding the AIC framework and its associated safety risks.Comer warned that the mechanism creates a dangerous loophole:“We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives.”Comer warned that federal legislation could be introduced to directly preempt state-level AI efforts.
Article Summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned against a legislative proposal in Delaware that would permit autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents to legally manage and operate corporate entities. The proposal has sparked sharp backlash from federal lawmakers like Representative James Comer (R-Ky), chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

Article Title: Oracle troubles aggravate as Microsoft scraps 3-year-old deal; comes as software giant rethinks cloud partnerships; renting computing from Oracle reportedly became less useful as ...
Article Text:
Microsoft 'refuses' to expand Texas data center deal with Nscale

Microsoft is phasing out an artificial intelligence (AI) computing partnership with Oracle Corp after choosing not to renew a 2023 agreement, Bloomberg has reported, citing people familiar with the matter. According to the report, Microsoft has steadily deactivated rented server capacity in recent months. The Oracle-hosted machines relied on older generations of Nvidia Corp. chips that no longer align with Microsoft's current computing requirements. The shift highlights growing industry unease surrounding hardware obsolescence; research firm Gartner Inc. has warned that aggressive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure risk significant write-downs as faster, more efficient chips enter the market.The loss of capacity utilization compounds existing headwinds for Oracle. Substantial capital outlays toward AI data center construction have driven the company’s free cash flow into negative territory, leaving its credit rating hovering just one level above junk status. Oracle’s stock has fallen by more than half since reaching a high in June.Neither company disclosed the total financial value of the contract when it was announced in 2023 to support Microsoft’s AI-powered Bing search engine, and Bloomberg was unable to determine its full scale.The wind-down follows an earlier report by Business Insider indicating that separate negotiations to lease additional Oracle capacity broke down in June this year.Oracle shares dropped roughly 3% following the news. An Oracle spokesperson stated that customer demand for its AI infrastructure remains robust, including for earlier-generation hardware. The non-renewal comes as Microsoft actively reviews more than $80 billion in outside cloud computing commitments across providers including CoreWeave, Nscale, and Nebius Group. Company executives have grown increasingly dissatisfied with escalating expenses and operational delays across these third-party agreements, Bloomberg reported. The tech giant recently passed on an option to expand an Nscale deployment in Texas, coming just weeks after it withdrew from a planned Nscale site in the UK.Microsoft will reportedly not exercise an option to more than double the size ​of its existing agreement with AI cloud provider Nscale to rent more ‌computing power at a Texas data center. According to a report in The Financial Times, a potential deal extension would have been ​worth tens of billions of dollars for Nscale. The companies struck ​a deal in 2025 for Nscale to deploy around 200,000 Nvidia AI chips under ​an expanded agreement with Microsoft across its data centers in Europe and the US.The development comes weeks ‌after ⁠Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's flagship data center project in Loughton, Essex, after power connection delays pushed its expected supply date into the 2030s.

According to the report, Microsoft has steadily deactivated rented server capacity in recent months. The Oracle-hosted machines relied on older generations of Nvidia Corp. chips that no longer align with Microsoft's current computing requirements.

OKXICE’s plan for blockchain-based stock trading meets rising corporate resistance.
