OKXICE proposed using that technology to offer trading beyond conventional stock-market hours.The venture comes after a temporary exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission in September. It allows qualifying platforms to trade tokenised stocks without registering as national securities exchanges, under certain conditions.Those conditions include notifying a company before offering shares tokenised by an unaffiliated third party and giving it an opportunity to object. The SEC also requires qualifying tokens to provide the same rights and privileges as equivalent traditional shares.According to Fortune, companies have 30 days from the date they receive notice to object and block their inclusion on the platform.Fortune reported that Boeing and ServiceNow joined the objection list this week, following Apple, Home Depot, and GE Vernova the day before.The resistance also extended beyond the venture’s original selection. Article Title: Nvidia is providing billions of dollars to expand advanced AI chip-packaging capacity at a Taiwanese supplier as a manufacturing bottleneck threatens to slow production of powerful processors
Article Text:
AI chip

Supply cracks at TSMC force chipmakers to look elsewhere

Why packaging now commands half the value

The rise of panel-level packaging

Nvidia is reportedly pouring billions of dollars into expanding advanced chip-packaging capacity at a Taiwanese supplier as severe manufacturing bottlenecks threaten to slow the delivery of high-performance artificial intelligence (AI) processors. The move comes as the global race to build AI infrastructure has unleashed unprecedented capital into advanced packaging – a stage of semiconductor manufacturing once viewed as routine, but now standing as the primary choke point in producing next-generation hardware.Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) currently dominates the market for the most sophisticated packaging technologies, primarily Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS). This method mounts individual silicon dies, such as processors and high-bandwidth memory, onto a shared base so they can transfer data at high speeds.CoWoS is essential for processors designed by Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, as well as custom silicon created by major cloud providers. However, TSMC’s limited packaging capacity has left chip designers scrambling to find alternatives.To bypass the squeeze, Nvidia is providing billions of dollars in financing to expand CoWoS capacity at Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL), a subsidiary of Taiwan’s ASE Technology, news agency Reuters cited an industry executive familiar with the situation, as saying.Notably, Nvidia is not alone in funding external capacity. Rival AMD has announced plans to invest more than $10 billion across Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem, striking partnerships with ASE, SPIL and Powertech Technology.“I think CoWoS and advanced packaging are super important for our high-performance computing going forward. TSMC has been an incredible partner in advanced packaging, and we're going to continue to do more together. And yes, we do need more capacity overall,” AMD CEO Lisa Su told Reuters during an October visit to Taipei.For decades, packaging was an afterthought aimed at encasing chips in plastic or ceramic to protect them and connect them to circuit boards. “Packaging was always that thing that you just didn't worry about,” former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger, now a partner at Playground Global, said recently in Taipei. That dynamic has flipped as shrinking transistors onto single silicon slabs becomes increasingly difficult and expensive. Today's GPUs and CPUs frequently combine anywhere from 10 to 20 distinct chips into a single package. Gelsinger estimates advanced packaging could eventually account for as much as half of a chip’s total value.AI chips rely heavily on this integration because training and running large models requires immense amounts of data to move between compute dies and memory banks without delay.TSMC’s tight lines have created major openings for secondary packaging firms like Taiwan’s Powertech Technology (PTI).“Everyone is looking for a solution outside TSMC. They don't want to rely entirely on TSMC,” Powertech Chairman D.K. Tsai said in August.PTI is betting on panel-level packaging, which processes chips on wide rectangular panels instead of conventional round silicon wafers. The format fits more units per run and cuts material waste – a key benefit as AI chips grow physically larger.PTI is collaborating with AMD and Broadcom to prove the viability of panel packaging for large-scale AI applications. Powertech also plans to invest $400 million in an advanced packaging joint venture with Broadcom in Singapore, targeting production by 2028.
Article Summary: N Nvidia is reportedly pouring billions of dollars into expanding advanced chip- packaging capacity at a Taiwanese supplier. The move comes as severe manufacturing bottlenecks threaten to slow the delivery of high-performance artificial intelligence (AI) processors. TSMC’s limited packaging capacity has left chip designers scrambling to find alternatives.

Article Title: Goldman Sachs bans thousands of employees from using Claude Code and GitHub; company says: After a period of experimentation, we put them in the hands of those...
Article Text:
No more vibe coding for Goldman traders

Goldman's CIO was cheering vibe coding by traders in July

Goldman's AI policy reflects a wider Wall Street rethink

Goldman Sachs has cut off most of its staff from advanced AI coding tools, and not everyone at the bank is pleased. Access to tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub is now limited to engineers, according to internal guidance updated in October and seen by Bloomberg. Traders, bankers and other non-technical employees, many of whom had been using these tools for months, have lost access.The bank says the call came after it looked at productivity and risk. A Goldman spokesperson, Nick Carcaterra, told Bloomberg that the firm offers certain AI tools to staff so it can figure out where they work best. Once that trial period ends, the tools go "in the hands of those who are best suited to leverage them," he said.There is one exception. The rule does not apply to strats, Goldman's term for employees who sit between trading, quantitative research and software engineering.Traders seem to feel the change most. According to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg, some had been using the tools to track client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and put together written and graphic content. On a trading desk, losing that kind of speed is felt quickly.The reversal stands out because Goldman had been openly encouraging this. In July, chief information officer Marco Argenti spoke about vibe coding by traders and bankers. He described non-technical staff building their own fixes with AI and passing them to one of the firm's 12,000 engineers to refine.This is also not Goldman's first AI restriction. Earlier this year, the bank limited the use of Anthropic's Claude for its Hong Kong staff, though that rule applied only to that location.None of this means Goldman is stepping back from AI. It has built an in-house AI assistant that combines models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google parent Alphabet. In May, John Waldron, seen as the likely successor to CEO David Solomon, compared the bank to an assembly line run by people and said much of that work could be automated.Goldman isn't the only bank rethinking how its staff use AI. Firms across Wall Street are spending millions of dollars on these tools while also dealing with cybersecurity worries, rising bills and uneven productivity gains. Working out who should use what has become a task of its own.JPMorgan Chase said in July it wanted employees to match models to tasks, so the priciest option isn't used for something as basic as summarising an analyst report. The idea is to keep costs in check without slowing people down.Goldman's move follows a similar line, applied to coding assistants. Instead of opening every tool to every employee, the bank is deciding which roles need them and limiting access to those roles.For now, that means engineers and strats. The traders who had built daily workflows around Claude Code and GitHub will have to find another way to get that work done.
Article Summary: Goldman Sachs has cut off most of its staff from advanced AI coding tools. Access to tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub is now limited to engineers. Traders, bankers and other non-technical employees have lost access. Goldman says the call came after it looked at productivity and risk.

The law targets what it calls “psychologically exploitative features” that could cause children to check social media compulsively, including personalised recommendations and videos that play automatically.It would require platforms to prevent users younger than 16 from accessing those features, with penalties for non-compliance. It also provides for deleting children’s accounts that retain the prohibited features.The law is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027, unless a court intervenes. Google, Meta and TikTok filed their separate challenges on Wednesday, the report claims.The companies argue the law violates the First Amendment, which protects freedom of speech, and Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, which broadly shields online platforms from liability for user-posted content.Meta spokesman Edward Patterson said the law would allow the government toand undermine the company’s ability to recommend age-appropriate content to children.Google said YouTube already restricted some features for minors, including autoplay on children’s accounts, and allowed parents to disable its short-form video feed, Shorts.said José Castañeda, a Google spokesman.TikTok said in its lawsuit that choosing which videos to show involvedprotected by free-speech rights.Supporters of the legislation argue that the challenge is about preserving features that keep young users engaged.said Brooke Istook, chief executive of the Heat Initiative, a tech-accountability advocacy organisation.California Attorney General Rob Bonta’s office said it was reviewing the lawsuits and remained committed to defending the state’s online child-protection laws.

Goyal answers doctors’ criticism with $20 million of his own money

Deepinder Goyal says Temple was never meant to be his next big bet. In a vision note titled “Humanity’s Last Personal Device”, the Zomato founder writes that he began building a health wearable as a weekend project while he was still CEO of Eternal, the company formerly known as Zomato. That project led to an engineering breakthrough, and the breakthrough is what pulled him out of Eternal to build Temple full-time.The note answers a question Goyal raised himself on X earlier in the day. Many people, he wrote, wanted to know why he would leave a roughly $35 billion company he founded 18 years ago to chase a niche health wearable. He conceded that it doesn’t sound like a rational move.Goyal’s reasoning starts with a grievance. He argues that privacy is a basic human right, and that every voice AI device sold as the next computing interface breaks it the moment its microphone switches on, because a mic records everyone in the room. He writes that he hates it when people walk into meetings with him with their AI note-taker running.Temple is his workaround. Instead of a mic, it reads the vibrations of the wearer’s voice through motion sensors, so it hears the person wearing it and nobody else. Goyal wrote, with an expletive, that there wasn’t even a word for that, so Temple invented one: “roomdeaf”.He is just as particular about what Temple won’t do. Goyal calls it a companion and not an assistant, because it will not shop for you and will stick to tasks that don’t need a screen.Personal devices, in his view, should get out of the way. He also writes that he sees Temple serving humanity in the space age, and suggests a few Black Mirror episodes as a reference for where it could go.Not everyone is sold. A section of Indian doctors has questioned Temple’s health claims on X, and Goyal replied with a seven-point post addressed to them.His first argument was commercial. Temple offers 14-day, no-questions-asked returns, which he noted even Apple doesn’t offer in India, so a device that failed to deliver would be exposed within days. He said Temple has cost $30 million so far, $20 million of it his own, and that a few thousand units would recover only a fraction of that. A scam that pays nothing, he wrote, isn’t one anyone would run.Then he made it personal. Goyal said he has enough money to last generations and would not stake a reputation built over 20 years on a quick buck. Temple’s employees invested in a round a few months ago, he added, and the round being raised now is mostly made up of customers.On the science, he pointed to Whoop, which shipped its band in 2015 and published validation a few years later. Temple’s pre-prints are coming, Goyal said, and its most groundbreaking features are still under wraps. He signed off by telling the doctors to keep raging if he hadn’t convinced them.Goyal calls Temple “a project, not a product” and says health remains its north star. Temple 01 ships in early 2027 with both AI and health features, pre-orders are open, and he is already talking about what Temple 20 might look like.The move he admits doesn’t look rational now has his money and a 20-year reputation riding on it.
Article Summary: Deepinder Goyal built Temple around his dislike of AI devices. Goyal says he has enough money to last generations and would not stake a reputation built over 20 years on a quick buck. Temple 01 ships in early 2027 with both AI and health features, pre-orders are open.

Article Title: Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam 'attacked'; months after balloons full of acidic mixture were thrown; riot police called in
Article Text:
Protestors outside Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam

Why people are protesting against Microsoft data centre

A group of protestors stormed the construction site of a massive Microsoft data centre located on the outskirts of Amsterdam on Friday (November 6), escalating European demonstrations targeting large-scale technology infrastructure. The latest ‘attack’ takes place just months after activists targeted the same location with acid-filled balloons. Riot police have been deployed which made multiple arrests. The breach occurred near Sloterdijk in Amsterdam’s western port area, where work is underway on a major three-building complex intended for Microsoft.As per a Reuters witness, approximately 100 people breached the site’s boundaries. However, a spokesperson for activist campaign group Geef Tegengas told local broadcaster AT5 that around 500 demonstrators entered the grounds, with hundreds more remaining outside. As per local news portal AN5, several protesters entered the facility by cutting or breaking through perimeter fences, while others scaled an on-site construction crane.Dutch news agency ANP reported that police had initially blocked the demonstration march earlier in the morning. After the city’s mayor issued an order banning the gathering, marchers attempted to push through established police lines before heading toward the building grounds.Geef Tegengas, an advocacy group that campaigns against fossil fuels, is demanding an immediate and permanent halt to the development due to straining power grids. The group claims the completed data centre will consume an amount of electricity equivalent to every household in Amsterdam combined, warning that the power drawn by the facility will derail the construction of 30,000 planned local homes.The development consists of three separate towers, each reaching a height of 85 metres, all of which will be leased entirely by Microsoft. Initial plans were submitted back in 2016, preceding a municipal ban enacted by Amsterdam on new data centre builds inside the city.Microsoft data centre is repeatedly being targeted in coordinated European actionThe November 6th’s security breach follows previous hostile actions directed at the exact same location. In July, members of Extinction Rebellion targeted the perimeter, throwing balloons loaded with paint and an acidic mixture over the security fences.Interestingly, Friday's demonstration was organised as part of a coordinated, two-day wave of protest actions scheduled across multiple European nations on November 6 and November 7.The organisers of the demonstration claimed that they are not satisfied with the police’s actions. “They behaved disgracefully. There is a right to demonstrate in this country, and that is being completely disregarded; even the march to the data center was not facilitated.”
Article Summary: Protestors stormed the construction site of a massive Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Friday (November 6) Riot police have been deployed which made multiple arrests. The latest ‘attack’ takes place just months after activists targeted the same location with acid-filled balloons.
